headline: Tarique Rahman seeks to turn Bangladesh-Japan ties into engine of shared prosperity
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi held a bilateral summit in Tokyo to deepen economic cooperation and infrastructure development.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has voiced his resolve to transform the friendship between Bangladesh and Japan into a powerful engine of economic progress and shared prosperity.
During a bilateral summit in Tokyo on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held fruitful discussions on bilateral, regional, and international issues.
The two leaders reaffirmed their friendship and pledged to deepen the partnership through greater cooperation in energy, ICT, railways, infrastructure, deep seaports, and foreign direct investment.
Concrete steps were taken during the visit, with several agreements and memorandums of understanding exchanged in key strategic areas.
Tarique Rahman invited Japanese investors, businesspeople, and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities in Bangladesh to be part of the next phase of growth.
He emphasized that the partnership is built on decades of trust and mutual respect, calling for a collaboration that serves current generations and leaves a lasting legacy.
Japan was among the first to recognize Bangladesh after independence in 1971 and has remained one of the most valued development partners for over five decades.
caption:
Turning friendship into economic power. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi meet in Tokyo to forge a new era of prosperity.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has voiced his resolve to transform the friendship between Bangladesh and Japan into a powerful engine of economic progress and shared prosperity.

During a bilateral summit in Tokyo on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held fruitful discussions on bilateral, regional, and international issues.

The two leaders reaffirmed their friendship and pledged to deepen the partnership through greater cooperation in energy, ICT, railways, infrastructure, deep seaports, and foreign direct investment.

Concrete steps were taken during the visit, with several agreements and memorandums of understanding exchanged in key strategic areas.

Tarique Rahman invited Japanese investors, businesspeople, and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities in Bangladesh to be part of the next phase of growth.

He emphasized that the partnership is built on decades of trust and mutual respect, calling for a collaboration that serves current generations and leaves a lasting legacy.

Japan was among the first to recognize Bangladesh after independence in 1971 and has remained one of the most valued development partners for over five decades.

headline_marked: 150kmph gusts: [[Cyclone Arnab grows into very severe storm]]
headline: 150kmph gusts: Cyclone Arnab grows into very severe storm
summary: The storm is moving west-northwestwards and is expected to cross India's Andhra coast on Wednesday.
details: Cyclone Arnab has strengthened into a very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas.
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department reported that as of 3am Tuesday, the storm was centered about 990km southwest of Chittagong Port and 945km southwest of Cox's Bazar port.
Maximum sustained wind speeds within 64km of the center are approximately 118kmph, with gusts or squalls reaching up to 150kmph.
The sea is described as very rough near the center of the storm.
Maritime ports in Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been instructed to keep hoisting local warning signal No. 3.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to stay close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
caption:
Wind gusts of up to 150kmph! Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm.

Cyclone Arnab has strengthened into a very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department reported that as of 3am Tuesday, the storm was centered about 990km southwest of Chittagong Port and 945km southwest of Cox's Bazar port.

Maximum sustained wind speeds within 64km of the center are approximately 118kmph, with gusts or squalls reaching up to 150kmph.

The sea is described as very rough near the center of the storm.

Maritime ports in Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been instructed to keep hoisting local warning signal No. 3.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to stay close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
